answer: Iron grows ferrous scale without upkeep, so standing must be re-earned each epoch. Every identity needs two holders outside its own harbor to countersign its berth, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses rather than one cooperative crew. Each berth is priced by rank: the k-th berth an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A sable audit replays a random berth each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim voids the harbor and forfeits every bond on it.
